summary: Takehiro Sueki was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1942–1945). He held academic posts at the University of Electro-Communications (~1949–1959), the University of Tokyo (~1959–1982), and Toyo University (~1982–1992).

Takeo Hibino was a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology who studied at Kyoto University (~1933–1936). He worked at Kyoto University's Institute for Research in Humanities and university faculty (1936–1977), later becoming a professor at Otemon Gakuin and Otemae universities.
Takeo Warita is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Toyo University from around 1964 to 1975 under Giyu Nishi.

Takeshi Fujii is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Delhi and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. He spent his career at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies from 1987, becoming professor in 2001 and professor emeritus in 2021.

Takeshi Karashima was a Sinologist who studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1924–1927). He held posts at Keijo Imperial University (~1928–1945), Sagami Women's University (~1951–1967), Showa Women's University, and Kamakura's library.

Takeshi Umehara was a scholar of philosophy, Japanology, and religious studies who studied at Kyoto University under Tokuryu Yamauchi. He held academic posts at Ritsumeikan University, Kyoto City University of Arts, and directed the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.

Takeshiro Kuraishi was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1918–1921). He served as a professor at Kyoto University (~1939–1949) and held a post at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1958).

Takezo Kaneko was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji. He held faculty posts at Hokkaido University, the University of Tokyo (~1950–1966), International Christian University (~1966–1976), and Seikei University (~1976–1983).
Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Po Lu Khenpo Dorjé. He succeeded Trulshik Rinpoche Ngawang Chökyi Lodrö in 2012.
Takudo Ishikawa is a Buddhist studies scholar. He has held positions as a researcher at the Research Institute of Jodo Shu (attested 2005) and as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 2015).

Takushu Sugimoto is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology scholar who completed his PhD at Tohoku University under scholars including Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha. He taught at Kanazawa University (~1980–2000, professor emeritus ~2000), Komazawa University (attested 1990), and Kinjo University (~2000).

Tampalawela Dhammaratana is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from the University of Kelaniya, University of Paris under Jean-François Lyotard, and Paris-Sorbonne University under Michel Hulin. He also completed postdoctoral studies at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Tan Chung is a historian and Sinologist who earned his PhD from Visva-Bharati University. He served as Professor of Chinese at the University of Delhi (~1964–1978) and chaired the Department of Chinese and Japanese Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1978–1994).
Tan Poh Beng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College (attested 2015) under the supervision of Charles Willemen and Tilak Kariyawasam.
Tan Sitong was a Chinese scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under Wang Zhengyi (~1895–1898) and Yang Renshan (~1896–1898).

Tan Yun-shan was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under teachers including Taixu and Kshitimohan Sen, taught at Lida Academy (~1923–1927), and served as Professor of Chinese Studies at Visva-Bharati University (~1937–1968).

Tanero Sasakawa was a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and Japanology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896). He later held posts at Toyo University and Meiji University (~1921–1944).

Tansen Sen is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Peking University and earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair, later holding a post at Baruch College (attested 2003).
Tanso Hirose was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kamei Juku (~1797–1801) and under Hodo, and went on to found Kangien in 1801.

Tanzan Hara was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Yushima Seido and Shoheizaka Gakumonjo. He served in the Ministry of Religion, became Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Tokyo (1879), and superintendent at Komazawa University (1891).
